title: 2003 AMC 12B Problem 13
statement: An ice cream cone consists of a sphere of vanilla ice cream and a right circular cone that has the same diameter as the sphere. If the ice cream melts, it will exactly fill the cone. Assume that the melted ice cream occupies \(75\%\) of the volume of the frozen ice cream. What is the ratio of the cone’s height to its radius?

solutions.text:
Let \(r\) be the common radius and \(h\) the cone’s height. The melted ice cream fills the cone, so \[ \frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h. \]

This simplifies to \(\pi r^3 = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h,\) so \(h = 3r,\) a ratio of \(3 : 1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The sphere and cone share the same radius \(r;\) sphere volume is \(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\)
Set \(75\%\) of the sphere’s volume equal to the cone’s volume \(\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\)
